facts.statement: Fossils of Kimmerosaurus have been found in England and Norway.
facts.quote: It is known from remains found in England and Norway.

facts.statement: The holotype of Kimmerosaurus is a partial skull (NHMUK R.8431) that was previously classified as Cryptoclidus eurymerus.
facts.quote: The holotype is NHMUK R.8431, a partial skull previously referred to Cryptoclidus eurymerus.

facts.statement: Peter Langham discovered the holotype and a second specimen at Endcome Bay, Dorset, in 1976, leading to the species name Kimmerosaurus langhami.
facts.quote: It was discovered alongside the second specimen by Peter Langham at Endcome Bay, Dorset in 1976 and was named as Kimmerosaurus langhami by Brown (1981b).

facts.statement: Two additional specimens were assigned to Kimmerosaurus in 1986: one found by Peter Langham in 1976 and another found by R. Damon in Weymouth around 1884.
facts.quote: NHMUK PV R 10042, a skull and five cervical vertebrae, was also discovered in 1976 by Peter Langham, while BNMH R.1978 was discovered in Weymouth by R. Damon around 1884 before it was donated to the British Museum in 1890; both specimens were assigned to Kimmerosaurus in 1986.

facts.statement: A more complete specimen (EC K2134) was discovered in the Etches Collection in 2015 and assigned to Kimmerosaurus by Roberts et al. in 2025.
facts.quote: A more complete Kimmerosaurus specimen from the Etches Collection, EC K2134 (consisting of the skull roof, brain case, dentary, teeth, hyoid, and vertebrae), was discovered on 7 March 2015 and was assigned to the genus by Roberts et al. (2025).

facts.statement: Three potential Kimmerosaurus specimens, mostly postcranial, were excavated in Svalbard between 1994 and 2009.
facts.quote: Three more potential specimens, including mainly postcranial material, of Kimmerosaurus were excavated in the Agardhfjellet Formation, Svalbard in 1994 and between 2004 and 2009.

facts.statement: Much of the description of Kimmerosaurus is based on its teeth, which are recurved and compressed from cheek to tongue side.
facts.quote: Because of this, much of the plesiosaur's description came from its teeth, which are recurved and buccolingually compressed (compressed cheek-side to tongue-side).

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Kimmerosaurus has eight teeth, while each ramus of the jaw has thirty-six teeth.
facts.quote: The premaxilla has only eight teeth, while there are thirty-six teeth on each ramus.

facts.statement: The skull of Kimmerosaurus is similar to Cryptoclidus but is much broader.
facts.quote: The overall skull of Kimmerosaurus is similar to Cryptoclidus but much more broad.

facts.statement: Kimmerosaurus is classified as the sister taxon of Cryptoclidus within the family Cryptoclididae.
facts.quote: Kimmerosaurus was placed into Cryptoclididae as the sister taxon of Cryptoclidus.

facts.statement: Kimmerosaurus fossils are found in the Kimmeridge Clay Formation near Kimmeridge, Dorset, England.
facts.quote: Kimmerosaurus fossils are found in the Kimmeridge Clay Formation near the village of Kimmeridge, in Dorset, England.

facts.statement: Kimmerosaurus likely ranged across much of the modern-day Jurassic Coast in southern England.
facts.quote: This animal may have ranged through much of what is now the Jurassic Coast, a World Heritage Site in the southern United Kingdom.

facts.statement: Kimmerosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 154.8 to 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether Kimmerosaurus fossils might actually represent the missing skull of the similar plesiosaur Colymbosaurus due to a lack of post-cranial remains.
facts.quote: It is this lack of any post-cranial fossils, and the bone similarities that has led to the belief that Kimmerosaurus fossils could be the missing head of Colymbosaurus, a similar plesiosaur with no known skull fossils.
